publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Opening Ceremony by COVEICYDET-UV-IEEE representatives

articleTitle: Low Cost Greenhouse Monitoring System Based on Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: It is a well-known situation that nowadays people are opting for organic food grown in an ecological way to reduce carbon footprint and damage to the environment. Ecology is suffering because of the use of pesticides and crop protection chemicals due to the damage caused to the flora and fauna in the environment where the crops are being cultivated. Combined with this, people are trying to get the freshest vegetables, fruits, and even flowers. Because of these situations, it is more common nowadays to find people trying to grow their food, or plants that they can't get in the place they live. For this, it is useful to use tools that can help the growth of these plants and make the job easier, but usually, greenhouses controllers are expensive and unnecessary due to the size of the home plantations. The creation of a low-cost greenhouse prototype that can be used in houses or small farms to help the people grow their crops and its comparison with current commercial systems are presented.

articleTitle: Detection of misalignment in motor via transient current signature analysis
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Motor Current Signature Analysis (MCSA) is a technique which can detect different types of faults such as misalignment, broken rotors, and internal and external bearings. The MCSA uses the current of the motor to detect a difference when the motor is healthy or it start to fails. The main goal of this work is to show how this technique is applied to detect misalignment by using the transient current of the rotor and to verify its operation by applying it to an experimental prototype.

articleTitle: Low Cost CO Detector Integrated with IoT
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This article presents a low cost project focused on detecting carbon monoxide in the environment and warning the user, based on the usage of the MQ-7 sensor, a loudspeaker (active buzzer) and the integrated circuit ESP8266. By means of the mobile application Blynk, the prototype will display the carbon monoxide levels in the environment in real time on your mobile device. If the concentration of carbon monoxide exceed 25 particles per million a loudspeaker will ring and send an alert to the mobile device instructing the people to leave the room, because this level of carbon monoxide concentration can be harmful or lethal to human health. The objective is to monitor the areas where it is possible a harmful concentration of carbon monoxide and ensure that people can leave in time before their health is in danger.

articleTitle: Programming logical controllers using remote labs and virtual reality
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper presents a project which consisted in teaching how to program logic controllers (PLCs) in the laboratory practices of Logical Automatisms through the technology of remote laboratories at Tecnológico de Monterrey. It is an educational innovation that aims to develop basic programming skills of a PLC in which the students design the automation lines using different methods such as Karnaugh maps and Grafcet. The obtained results and algorithms can be simulated using different Virtual Reality Devices available in all campuses of the university. Once the correctness of the obtained designs is verified properly, they can be taken to the real remotely located equipments which are available by telecommunication technologies developed internally. In campus Tampico, for instance, the real PLC is connected to a scale elevator that is precisely controlled by the program developed by the student. The behavior of the elevator is monitored by a set of web cameras controlled by the user via the Internet. This teaching tool was very useful for “learning by doing”. Such remote laboratories had prove theirselfs as an excellent high performance and low-cost alternative comparing to the traditional ones.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Wireless Network Based on ZigBee Technology Using XBee Modules
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: computer aided instruction; Internet of Things; wireless sensor networks; renewable energy sources; microcontrollers; educational institutions; teaching; design engineering; building management systems; photovoltaic power systems.

articleTitle: Wireless Sensor Network Prototype to Monitor the Condition of Holding Furnaces in the Aluminum Casting Plant
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Currently in the industry, higher production levels are required every day, for this reason, it is essential that the machinery used for production is always in optimal conditions which will consequently increase the production efficiency. Due to this, the continuous monitoring of the machinery's condition has become a strong strategy to maximize production time. Due to the growing demand to monitor technologies, this document proposes the development of a prototype that allows monitoring the condition of maintenance furnaces used in a foundry plant to keep melted aluminum at a temperature between 600°c and 620°c. The electrical current consumed by the resistors that maintain the temperature in melted aluminum is measured through a Wireless Sensors Network (WSN). Through this network, it is possible to monitor this type of machinery continuously and remotely, allowing awareness of the industry's wellbeing thanks to the application of the Industrial Internet of Things.

articleTitle: Proposal of a Computer System for Vocational Guidance with Data Mining
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Scholar desertion is a serious problem in the university environment. Different references have reported that one key factor causing this problem in Mexico, and other Latin America countries, beyond the economic problem, is poor vocational guidance or the lack of it. In this document, we present a proposal of a computational system that helps students to determine the possibilities of finishing their studies when they choose a university career. To do this, the use of data mining and Knowledge Discovery in Databases techniques is proposed. The proposed framework includes a collection of a large database fed for users using digital forms, for a long period of time. In this way, the system will learn about successful or failed cases, and it could make suggestions to new aspirants. In this paper, the plan to follow is showed and some considerations are discussed. Also, we discuss some suggestions, observations, and limitations that the presented system could present when implemented, directed to monitoring the process experienced by students.

articleTitle: A review on quantum dot solar cells: properties, materials, synthesis and devices
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Quantum dot semiconductors have gain great attraction for the development of high efficiency solar cells due to remarkable optoelectronic properties such as tunable bandgap, multiple exciton generation (MEG) and high extinction coefficient. Despite quantum dot solar cells having theoretical power conversion efficiency of about 66%, actual maximum efficiency is only 16.6%. So, it is important to further understand the relations between properties, elements composition, material structures and synthesis methods, as well as devices architectures in order to propose strategies addressed to close the gap between actual and theoretical power conversion efficiencies. This article exposes the advances related to materials and methods of synthesis, and their impact in quantum dot properties. It also introduces some recent quantum dot solar cells designs.

articleTitle: Comparative study of competences in higher education students
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In essence, students do not know the necessary skills, as well as their training needs required for their entry to the higher level. At present, it is essential to have, at least, the basic skills for digital literacy. In this article, we propose a quantitative and qualitative research about the current situation of the digital competences of new students of the Faculty of Accounting and Administration of the Universidad Veracruzana, as well as an important comparison between educational programs to understand the reality of how is their training in the field of digital knowledge at the lower immediate level of education. A methodology is proposed from the conceptual and theoretical part allowing to carry out the conceptualization, under a deductive process, carrying out the process of conceptualization to the operationalization following the phases of theoretical representation of the concept, specification of the concept for the identification of the dimensions and from each dimension its indicators, resulting in an instrument with validity and reliability that was applied to a stratified sample to identify digital competences in the five evaluated dimensions, all so that, based on the diagnosis, strategies can be generated in Universities to identify the competences of new students and then expand their knowledge about this area, in such a way that it allows them to have information for making decisions regarding the training and qualification to improve their learning processes.

articleTitle: Graphical User Interface as a Preliminary Structural Design Educative Tool for a Vessel
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: When a student of naval engineering is introduced to issues related to structures of a ship, it is difficult to understand vessel concepts. A graphical user interface (GUI) that helps visually understand the baseline of a ship depending on the pressure, the gravity and tanks level is adequate to accomplish the task with partial ease, quickly and also enjoy the learn experience. This paper describes the development of a user interface for its implementation in the naval Engineering Educational, is designed with structured and modular programming using open source software MyOpenLab©. The goal of this work is calculated longitudinal resistance of the boats, obtaining the diagrams of shear force and bending moment.

articleTitle: EOG-based interface and speech recognition for wheelchair control
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Mobility problems are a growing international medical concern. We developed a prototype to help patients with paralysis of the lower extremities to control a wheelchair using Electrooculography (EOG) signals and the voice signal. EOG signal can control the direction of movement, while the voice signal processing controls the on and off the wheelchair. The prototype is a scalable, portable, compact and inexpensive with acceptable results with a noninvasive design.

articleTitle: Mobile Positioning for IoT-based Bus Location System Using LoRaWAN
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This article aims to describe, explain and propose the implementation of a Mobile LoRaWAN Gateway device and how this can use the benefits of the LoRaWAN communication protocol and system architecture along with IoT to bring a new solution for applications which need a mobile alternative, or which not have the resources to support a conventional LoRaWAN gateway solution. The purpose of this project is to test the capabilities of the LoRaWAN taking a different approach and prove its advantages against other similar solutions that do not use LoRaWAN for some applications.

articleTitle: A Portable and Wireless System for Monitoring Hand Tremors in Parkinson's Disease Patients
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this study we present the development of a portable system to measure tremors in the hands of Parkinson's patients. During development, samples were taken from 30 patients previously diagnosed, with Parkinson's disease and 10 healthy controls. The data was sent by Bluetooth to the Matlab platform for further analisys. The results obtained are frequencies between 4-8Hz of patients with Parkinson's disease and frequencies below 3Hz in healthy patients.

articleTitle: Comparative of wind systems vs photovoltaic for the implementation in the electric network of Veracruz Port
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this paper presents the feasibility between t comparison of implementation photovoltaic solar systems a<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sub>wind systems for power generation in the port of Veracruz, for residential electricity supply connected to the CFE network, starting from the characterization of the renewable resource, the geographical delimitation, characterizing the demand f a particular case with respect to a year and analyzing the generation of both systems and the Billings according to that generation. For this, factors have been analyzed such as solar radiation per peak solar hour, wind speed and direction for the year 2018 were analyzed by time measurements and electricity consumption data for a particular year. Finally, an analysis is presented don the feasibility of the best systems according to the results.

articleTitle: Zigbee Networks in Teaching Environments
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new field of application for wireless communication networks based on Zigbee Technology: educational environments. In the classroom, administrative activities are carried out as part of teaching. Hence, we suggest the implementation of a tool that will optimize the execution of these activities, as well as the time dedicated to them. In the proposed system, a coordinating node and several end nodes make use of Arduino boards and radiofrequency communication devices (XBee modules) to communicate during experiments or activities within a class. The design of the communication scheme allows the coordinating node to acquire and manage digital signals to interact with end users, even if they are physically dispersed in one or more classrooms. The coordinating node is associated with a graphical user interface desktop application from which the experiments carried out by the students can be directed with the aid of the final nodes and a test plate. The proposed design has up to eight nodes in its initial stage. Additionally, the proposal is implemented in a basic Digital electronics class.

articleTitle: Decreasing False Positive Detection of Gaussian Watermarks by Means of Fractional Calculus Principles
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Fractional calculus is a promising and rich area of study as many applications to engineering are under development. As a result, many authors proposed new approaches for solving diverse problems with success. In particular, we focus on revisiting a problem in the digital watermarking field: the detection of Gaussian watermarks in the spatial domain. The novelty of this work is that we show that the use of fractional calculus principles reduces the false positive rate of a Gaussian watermarks detector whereas keeping the complexity of the system almost low. Most systems detect Gaussian watermarks using different strategies that increase the system complexity, this motivates our work which goal is to address the detection problem with a simpler approach.

articleTitle: Implementation of fuzzy controller in different embedded systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This article presents the implementation of different embedded systems in the development of fuzzy logic for its application in the control of a furnace with measures to 100°C for the optimization of preheating in surface mounted devices. Fuzzy logic accepts multiple variables that the device must process efficiently, so it is very important to make the appropriate choice of the embedded system to achieve adaptability to any problem presented. In addition, the observations of the development of fuzzy logic within the program are discussed.

articleTitle: Comparison of Optimization Methods for Hybrid Renewable Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper shows the results obtained from the evaluation of two methods for the optimization of a Hybrid Renewable Energy System (HRES). The first consists of an algorithm developed in MATLAB. The second is a model developed in the HOMER tool. The potential of a renewable resources, the energy demand of the load and the costs of the components, are introduced for both methods. As a case study, it was considered an aquafarm located in the municipality of Alvarado, Veracruz, Mexico. The optimal system obtained with the MATLAB algorithm consists of a combination of a diesel generator, 64 batteries and a 32 kW photovoltaic (PV) array. On the other hand, the optimal system found with HOMER consists of a combination of a diesel generator, 64 batteries, a 3.5 kW wind turbine and a 32 kW PV array, like that obtained with the algorithm.

articleTitle: Indoor Fire Simulation with Avoidance Path Planning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Nowadays, the use of simulation is increasing widely because there is a high benefit comparing against it cost. Less physical space as well as other resources are needed in comparison with real scenarios. In addition, risks are avoided in dangerous environments. One example of these risk scenarios are buildings in flames. At this moment there exist different outdoor fire simulators, even, there exist a few simulators for fire in indoor scenarios. Although there exist different conditions that can not be controlled in all aspects and these conditions influence directly in the fires, an indoor fire can be simulated in a kind realistic way, showing rescue teams some of the propagation patterns and reducing risks at same time. In this work, an indoor fire simulator has been created to generate the propagation matrix for each one of the propagation steps. This matrix can be used later to test other algorithms such as explaining fire behavior or avoiding the fire trajectory.

articleTitle: Numerical Analysis of an Offshore Pratol Vessel to Work in the GoM Using the Finite Element Method
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: At new ship's design stages, an important requirement is to grant the structure safety during ship's operation. In this scenario, it is relevant to make a dynamic analysis to identify possible resonance conditions between the structure and the main excitation sources. This work is evaluating the dynamic analysis and the structural strength according to the recommendations from the classification society DNV GL for the Oceanic Patrol type OPV. The calculation of the RAO's was developed using the Motion Maxsurf software to evaluate it. The structure of a ship is analysed with different loading conditions. The vessel is considered as a beam, supported, on a wave of length equal to the length of the vessel whose ridge is in the hull girder, or on the same wave, but with the breast in the mainframe and it is crests forward and Stern. The structural strength of the main frame of a vessel by the Finite Element Method using the GeniE DNV GL software. The results are in good agreement for this patrol to navigate on the Gulf of Mexico.

articleTitle: The exoskeleton: Operation with electrostimulators for rehabilitation
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The exoskeleton is a mechanical device designed to help people suffering from motor disabilities in order to provide a better life experience, as well as a more complete rehabilitation through electro-stimulators that activate the muscles. This invention provides supports in both, the top and bottom of the body helping with the recovery of motor ability. electro-stimulators are based on the application of a massage through electrical pulses at specific points of the body. To perform a movement in the exoskeleton, the carrier must activate a small joystick which comes out with a signal that is amplified and becomes into microcontrollers that are programmed to activate the desired movement. One of the most important parts regarding movement by the hip which joins parts of the torso and legs.

articleTitle: Virtual Motion Detection Method Using Fuzzy Logic for an Embedded System
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This document presents a method that emulates virtual motion detection with non-invasive sensors for actuator control by using fuzzy logic, to determine the position of an object in three-dimensional space, as well as the direction of its movement. The design and analysis of the fuzzy algorithm were performed with MATLAB using fuzzy logic and by the method of implication Mamdani. An algorithm was generated for architecture with two-dimensional meshes of 10 ×10 sensors and actuators, the algorithm allows to modify the number of linguistic variables, however, for the results presented here, five values were considered. The process was divided into two stages, the first one evaluates individually the distance that each sensor detects, and the second one discriminates different detection areas according to the number of sensors activated. Finally, the viability of its possible implementation in an FPGA was suggested, which would carry out the corresponding operations of the algorithm to generate different levels of amplification in the actuators. The results were analyzed employing test cases to generate the corresponding graphs.

articleTitle: An iterative method of constant slope for solution of nonlinear equations in electrical power systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this paper, a constant slope method is applied to solve nonlinear equations and calculate the Voltage and load flow in an electrical power system. In an electrical power system of N nodes, N-1 non-linear equations are established, and they are related; the power in each node, the admittance matrix and the nodal Voltage. These equations are solved with an iterative method of slope constant of five steps. The theoretical foundations of the method and convergence analysis it's included in the paper. The method is applied to different test systems and the results obtained show differences in the magnitude of the Voltage, ranging from 0.05% to 5.0%. Due to the formulation, the number of iterations is high, however, since only elementary algebraic operations are carried out, the execution time ranges between 16 and 180 milliseconds.

articleTitle: Design and characterization of liquid nanocapsules of rosemary oil (Rosmarinus officinalis L.)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Currently, plants are important to produce medicines and functional foods, as they are a source of bioactive compounds. One of the plants that have been investigated since ancient times is rosemary (Rosmarinus Officinalis L.). The essential oil of rosemary is a complex mixture of volatile compounds used in the food industry since it contains phenols, flavonoids, and terpenes. These molecules have antimicrobial, neuroprotective, antioxidant, and anti-inflammatory, as well as anti-tumor properties. Therefore, it is necessary to enhance the benefits that these bioactive compounds can provide through the production of nanoemulsions, which would increase the bioavailability and absorption of these. The main objective of the present work was to prepare and characterize oil/water (O/W) nanoemulsions of rosemary aqueous extract and essential oil elaborated by ultrasound. To achieve the nanoemulsions, the aqueous phase was to prepare by a liquid-solid extraction method (ratio 1:6), whereas 0.3% of essential oil as lipidic phase, using Tween 40 and Span 20 as surfactants. Nanoemulsions loaded with rosemary extracts were fabricated using surfactants blend with a hydrophilic-lipophilic balance (HLB), ranging from 10 to 14 with a high-power ultrasound. The analysis of the appropriate parameters was performed out by evaluating the particle size, zeta-potential and polydispersion index. The mean diameters (Z-average) of the dispersed particles containing rosemary extracts ranged from 50 to 437 nm and negative value of Z-potential. The results showed that the nanoemulsions with better characteristics are those of 12 HLB value and 1:1.5 oil: surfactant ratio. These results provide useful information for the design of delivery systems to encapsulate and stabilize lipophilic molecules.

articleTitle: Development of a Prototype for Ocular Monitoring with Infrared Light
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: By means of a prototype that consists of a camera, infrared LED, a computer will be presented a tool with which a person can interact with the medium. This work consists in the creation of the prototype and of the code for the detection of the pupil with which it will be possible that the user can interact with the interface.

articleTitle: Smoke Detection in Video using a Raspberry Pi
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Many different algorithms have been developed for smoke detection of in video. However, most of these algorithms have been implemented in simulations with specialized software or computers with high computational capacity. This article presents results of implementation of a method to smoke detection in video, which was implemented in a Raspberry Pi embedded computer using OpenCV library. This method proposes to use different smoke characteristics such as: movement, color, direction, growth, accumulation and a background subtraction method, so that movement detection is as optimal as possible to be able to detect early smoke presence and prevent a possible mishap. This algorithm was evaluated using 22 different videos obtaining up to 90.9% accuracy in smoke detection and up to 9.1% false positives, showing that proposed method obtains favorable results.

articleTitle: “Exergetic Analysis of a Brayton-Stirling Combined Cycle Operated with Biogas from a Swine Farm”
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: As part of the proposal to improve the use of waste heat from a CHP system with a gas microturbine, in a pork industry, the possibility of coupling and activating a Stirling engine was studied, which would be generating a Brayton combined cycle-Stirling. In the present work we present the exergy analysis that was carried out as part of the technical feasibility study. When the exergetic method is applied, it is possible to observe by means of a comparison with a first law analysis, that there may be considerable losses of useful energy, and that, if the appropriate strategies are proposed to correct them, they would improve the efficiency of the system. Seven scenarios were performed varying the percentage of coverage of the energy demand of the farm, which would allow to review the individual behavior of the equipment. In the exergy analysis performed it is possible to visualize the destruction of exergy of each component (Compressor, Heat recuperator, Chamber of combustion, Turbine and Stirling engine power transfer processes) in each of the evaluated alternatives, efficiencies of less than 50% were found, - against 70% of the analysis of the first law - it being possible to observe that the process carried out within the the combustion chamber has the highest irreversibilities regardless of the type of fuel used, followed by the transfer of energy from the exhaust gases to the Stirling engine head, another aspect that can be observed in comparison with the energy analysis is that the Fuel shows a greater value in the exergy than in the energy part. The results of the exergy evaluation of the cycle coincide with the results obtained for the gas turbine studys, where they show that about 70% of the destruction of the exergy is in charge of the combustion chamber. It is proposed as a recommendation derived from this exergy analysis the possibility of coupling two Striling motors for the proposed microturbine connected in parallel, and this would significantly increase the biogas yield and therefore the energy efficiency of the cycle. The global energy crisis has led to think about the progressive energy improvement by persistently developing innovation for the improvement of technologies that already exist. From the technological innovation the idea of this project is born, the design of a system for generating electric power through cogeneration technologies that have renewable energy as primary fuel, in this case biogas. This is the case of this pork company, there are biodigesters that treat organic manure waste produced by pigs and biogas is produced with these wastes. Biogas production per year is 160 m3 / hr and has approximately 70% methane among its chemical composition.

articleTitle: Temperature detection system applied to an electrical substation in Lima Norte
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Peru has had an annual growth in the electricity sector, being of the greatest consideration and importance, but in turn, it entails certain problems of electrical connectivity such as interruptions. In recent years there has been an average annual interruption time of 9 hours and 24 minutes; affecting economic and social aspects, which establishes a major problem in seeking to reduce losses in electricity supply. In this research work, a temperature detection system in electrical substations has been designed and implemented through the use of a microcontroller and temperature sensors, which automatically guarantee overload detection, as this is the main cause of the electrical connectivity interruptions, which is based on the detection of temperatures at certain points in substations, which will be used to compare the real values and generate alerts to the entities that regulate and give the respective maintenance. As a result of the observation and analysis of these electrical substations, the following temperatures were obtained at 28° C, 56° C and 75° C, to be used in the comparison and to define a state; the latter being the overheat alert value to prevent future interruption.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Adjustment of a Microwave Filtered Signal by using an Optical Bandpass Filter
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: A novel technique to increase the bandwidth of a microwave filtered signal situated at 7.17GHz is described. The filtered signal is obtained by means of a microwave photonic filter that employs in an advantageous manner the chromatic dispersion exhibited by optical fibers. In particular, a multimode laser diode associated to single mode-standard fiber is used. The use of an optical bandpass filter is proposed to modify the optical bandwidth of a multimode laser diode. Experimentally it is demonstrated that the optical bandwidth is changed from 6.69nm to a 2.2nm. As consequence, the bandwidth of the microwave filtered signal is varied from 385MHz to 1.19GHz. A Signal-to-Noise-Ratio of 15dB guarantees a good quality of this signal.

articleTitle: Visual level optimization for a device for detecting clandestine connections in low voltage lines in Lima-Perú
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Currently, the Distribution Company Governor of Lima North has low symbolic electrical networks with aerial and underground connections with an extension of 12,836. Four kilometers and with an energy loss of 8.24%. The company has carried out 128,000 inspections with which it has been able to invoice 50 GWh, however, a high incidence of electrical fraud has been found through clandestine or unauthorized connections, which are hidden causing non-technical losses, which are detected through the flow detectors, but have deficiencies in the accuracy for detection. This is why we propose the design of a reliable electrical flow meter system to improve the problems affected by a LED light sequence circuit, thus giving a more accurate measurement and being able to have control in inspections, as a result is obtained by an excellent implementation of the circuit that was simulated in the proteus software and put into practice in the streets of the city.

articleTitle: Towards team performance visualization in collaborative systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: There are efforts aimed at the detection of performance indicators in collaborative systems. However, they face the challenge of their visual representation for the adequate interpretation of the user. For its part, the information display area has a wide range of techniques and theories for the visual representation of data. Therefore, this paper explores the process and visualization techniques to represent performance indicators in collaborative systems. Also, describes the results of an exploratory test from which there is a trace of a positive effect on users that visualize the team performance indicators.

articleTitle: Implemented strategies for the saving of energy in a liquid sulfur tank: Case of the maritime terminal of Coatzacoalcos, Mexico
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The present work describes the reconstruction of a tank of liquid sulfur with a capacity of 7,500 metric tons, which has its interior serpentines operating as heat exchangers, the steam that flows into the coils exchanges heat with liquid sulfur. This tank is located in the Maritime Terminal of Storage and Distribution of Sulfur in the port of Coatzacoalcos, Mexico. The container had a useful life of more than 40 years and had high energy consumption for the exchange of heat between steam and sulfur. In addition, it had structural wear due to years of operation without adequate maintenance, which represented a technical and environmental risk. The objective of this work is to make the modifications corresponding to the tank specifically in the thermal insulation, which has been replaced by one with a lower coefficient of heat transfer and greater efficiency, the foundation is modified to guarantee a greater structural support, the traps of steam were replaced to take advantage of a greater heat transfer, the tank is reconstructed in its entirety (Base, walls and dome). With the modifications, steam consumption for the operation of the tank was reduced from approximately 14 tons to 11 tons of steam per day. In addition, the sulfur temperature increased from 126°C to 139 °C, this allows complying with export parameters abroad that are 133°C for sale.

articleTitle: Scenario Creation with Room Labelling: Iterative and Recursive Comparison
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In a lot of sciences is always necessary to determine the performance of new algorithms, profiling is a useful tool during the process of development and testing. Is very helpful to have a huge testing dataset to ensure that the proposed methodology is robust for a wide range of possible scenarios. In most of the public dataset the number of scenarios to probe new algorithms is limited and not standard, because of that, in this work is done a comparative between two ways to create scenarios with the characteristic before mentioned: The recursive and the iterative one.

articleTitle: Robotical Implementations of Collision-Free Path Planning for Terrestrial Systems using RGPPM
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Path planning has been considered as key part for expanding the intelligent properties because it faces the problem of finding collision-free motions for robot systems from one configuration to another. Resistive Grid Path Planning Methodology (RGPPM) is a novel and reduced CPU time modelling and simulation procedure for robotic motions planning. In this paper, robotical implementations of collision-free path planning using an emerging grid-based methodology is carried out by embedded systems applications and robot application framework.

articleTitle: Analysis of HfO2 effect on the electrical performance of a-SiGe:H TFTs using 2D numerical simulations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this manuscript, we analyze the hafnium oxide (HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>) effect as high k gate insulator on the electrical performance of planarized Hydrogenated Amorphous Silicon Germanium Thin Film Transistors, a-SiGe: H TFTs, in bottom-gate (BT), top-contact (TC) structure configuration, using 2D numerical simulations with Silvaco TCAD. Output and transfer characteristics of a-SiGe: H TFTs with two different gate insulators, SiO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>and HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub>, are simulated in order to extract the main DC electrical parameters. The simulated results indicate that a-SiGe: H TFTs with HfO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> present a reduced threshold voltage (V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</sub>), higher current drive, a higher transconductance (gm), a lower subthreshold slope (SS), and higher on/off current ratio, (I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</sub>/I<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">OFF</sub>). In addition, an AC analysis is performed to extract the cutoff frequency at unitary current gain (f<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">T</sub>) for different channel lengths.

articleTitle: Financing of Photovoltaic Systems for low consumption users
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In the present work an analysis was carried out for the financing of photovoltaic systems of residential users of low consumption within the subsidy scheme and financing funds through the Clean Energy Certificates (CEL's) in the Mexican Republic. Based on statistics of bimonthly average consumption, low consumption rates were used that concentrate the largest number of users; setting a limit of 250 kWh of consumption for each user and a photovoltaic production system with 4 panels of 300 Watts is calculated; from the result of the analysis it is obtained that this system can have a financing term of ten years instead of the subsidy to the payment of the invoicing. The surpluses of energy equivalent to CEL's obtained can be managed to enter the Wholesale Electricity Market (MEM) through a government trust.

articleTitle: Design and implementation of a third-order Chebyshev bandpass microstrip filter with coupled lines for digital television
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a third-order Chebyshev bandpass microstrip filter with coupled lines for the transmission of two channels of digital television, which are located at frequencies 524 and 536 MHz respectively, in the city of Hermosillo, Mexico. This filter focuses on the frequency of 530 MHz with a bandwidth of approximately 12 MHz. FR4 substrate with a relative permittivity of 4.3 and a width of 1.6 mm was used in its construction. Then, the parameters S11 and S21 of the filter were analyzed, characterized and validated.

articleTitle: Patch antenna design for UHF RFID systems
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Nowadays the use of RFID systems is increasing for different applications, which leads to a higher demand of antennas, since there is no perfect antenna capable of working with all frequencies. This document presents the design of a patch antenna with direct feed method with coaxial connector by means of mathematical equations; the results obtained by simulating it are also presented.

articleTitle: Virtual and Remote Experimentation in Database Learning
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: A virtual and remote experimentation platform was implemented for the learning of the Databases at the Universidad Veracruzana. The background of the laboratories where virtual and remote experimentations were carried out was investigated, as well as the theoretical foundation necessary to be able to carry out the design and implementation of a platform that supports the learning of the bases of data. This virtual experimentation platform was implemented through the Moodle tool as Virtual Educational Environment, which was hosted in the hosting called: Virtual Link where the theoretical knowledge of the database study program was developed. The instructional design considered elements as a unit of competence, development of the relevant content, evaluation and great diversity of Web 3.0 elements. We selected as a population to carry out the virtual platform use to students who were studying the educational experience of Data Bases in the Bachelor in Computer Systems Administration Xalapa. This project supports learning through the virtual and remote experimentation platform, as well as a methodology that allows the design, development and implementation of practical database exercises. The results show the dynamism and simplicity that virtual and remote experimentation can have for the teaching of databases, in addition to having achieved great acceptance by students because it is used through a mobile device.

articleTitle: Electronic Dispositive for Measure Corrosion Rate
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this research, a prototype was designed to measure the corrosion rate in situ using Arduino to program an potential value, to perform a sweep to obtain the electrochemical response in current [1], and using the Stern and Geary's formula to calculate the linear polarization resistance (LPR), after that is use the second faraday's law to obtain the corrosion rate. To make the Arduino system and the electronic circuit work together using a solar panel. The prototype measures the corrosion potential of the electrochemical cell where the working electrode was a 1018 steel, the Ag/AgCI was the reference electrode, the graphite was the counter electrode and a 3.5% NuCl solution was the electrolyte. The tests were achieved in the laboratory, but the purpose of the device is to measure the corrosion rate in-situ at water immersed and buried structures as pipelines.

articleTitle: Matrix array of CMOS photodetectors for brain transillumination
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The main structures of pn junction CMOS photodetectors are analyzed for the application in the transillumination technique with the purpose of analyzing organic materials. The selection of the right photodetector is made for the application of a matrix array for the integration of an integrated circuit for brain transillumination. An N-well / p-substrate photodiode designed in 0.5μm CMOS technology is presented, considering its spectral range of 700nm, also the depth of doping in the structure to improve photon collection. A first 24×24 μm photodiode was designed, an array of 5×5 photodiodes using the structure of the first photodiode, and finally a second arrangement of 5×5 using the above array.

articleTitle: Vehicles Location using Probabilistic Broadcasting in Mobile Ad Hoc Networks
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Mobile Ad Hoc Networks (MANETs) present a communication challenge since most of their nodes have low-performance hardware resources in a structureless environment. These nodes leave and join the network several times in short intervals. Thence, there is not a stable data link between all nodes. Various mechanisms, technics, protocols, and algorithms must be implemented to allow effective information sharing through the whole MANET. In this work, high-level architectonic design and an algorithm with a probabilistic schema are proposed in order to bring the capability to send information without control messages overload, through the use of low-level protocols and deciding when to forward a message. The message forwarding is determined by a counter schema that feeds the probabilistic algorithm. This solution allows a better performance due to sent packages reduction that does not saturate network bandwidth. Therefore this work contributes to risk mitigation related to Command, Control, and Communication (C3) center's workload. The above due to every node would have positioning capabilities provided by the use of common Wi-Fi Technology, a Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) and a visualization interface.

articleTitle: Energy Demand Assessment for water in the residential sector in Mexico
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The use of energy in the residential sector is of vital importance to satisfy basic needs and to improve the quality of life of the people. While there are several studies that determine the demand for energy by end uses, the most representative are cooking, air conditioning, lighting and refrigeration of food, however those uses that represent little demand for energy have not been studied and they end up adding in the category as other uses, such as the pumping of water that is essential for human survival. In this sense, the objective of this work is to estimate the electric energy demand required to pump water in the horizontal and vertical condominiums of Mexico for 2016 as a particular year. To estimate the demand for electricity by pumping water, it was decided to use a bottom-up type model that calculates energy consumption individually and by groups of houses, and then extrapolate the results at the national level. The proposed model uses statistical information to use an Engineering Method (MI). The work is developed by presenting a general overview of energy consumption in the residential sector by end use, the methodology for estimating the demand for electricity is shown, the construction of the model and the variables used are explained, the results presented by the model and finally recommendations are issued for subsequent projects.

articleTitle: Internet of Things: Low Cost Monitoring BeeHive System using Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Precision Beekeeping is an emerging research direction of Internet Things, based on a management strategy of individual monitoring of the colonies to minimize consumption resources and maximize the productivity of bee, is a challenging topic in the conditions of helping to add value to the apicultural chain, preserve the species, take care of the environment and contribute to the economic and social development of the territory. This document proposes an IoT system that can be applied into the hive to help beekeepers to get better control trough precision measurements. The need and importance of how this system can collaborate to carry out more in-depth studies in the region through precision beekeeping are presented too. Therefore this document proposes a system architecture that can help to increase the productivity and accuracy using sensors to measure humidity, temperature, and weight remotely to finally send this data from the hive to the third-party online Ubidots platform services.

articleTitle: PLATANO: Intelligent Technological Support Platform for Azuay province Farmers in Ecuador
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Faced with the evident growth of the gap between digitalization and agriculture, there is a search for optimal technologies to boost the development of this important economic activity. Therefore, this article presents a proposal for an IoT architecture for the integration of agricultural monitoring systems, through which it is possible to bundle different crop sensing networks. The general model of each of these subsystems leads to the sending of monitored data to a central server through the Internet, to later analyze and manage the information. Initially, the integration of cocoa, coffee, potato and an urban garden of different localities of Azuay, Ecuador is considered. This model seeks to involve small and medium farmers with technological solutions which, thanks to its integration, will facilitate the active participation of entities in charge of promoting agricultural production, generating a greater impact than that produced by a single particular monitoring network.

articleTitle: Study of harmonic content and influence of common electrical appliances used in residential installations
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In this paper, we report the findings derived from measurements in a typical residential installation in the state of Veracruz, Mexico. Common electrical appliances were studied individually and then measurements were made to the whole house installation using a digital analyser for the monitoring of harmonic distortion in voltage and current. Individual results were out of the norm specifications for several appliances, but it was found that the combination of them produced a less distorted home system.

articleTitle: Design and Modeling of a Microfluidic Device with Potential Application for Isolation of Circulating Tumor Cells
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Currently, cancer is a worldwide health problem causing around 8.8 million deaths in 2015. An approach to reduce the number of losses caused by cancer is the early detection and personalized treatment for each patient. Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) are derived from primary tumor tissues and transferred to other organs of the human body. The microfluidic devices have potential application to isolate CTCs from a blood sample using cell physical properties. In this paper, we present the design and modeling of a microfluidic device for separation of microparticles with sizes similar to CTCs in a continuous flow using computational fluid dynamic (CFD). The microfluidic device has two spiral microchannels with rectangular cross-sections (50μm height and 200 μm width). The device design has two isolation phases, in which the first phase is used to isolate particles larger than 18 μm. In the second phase, the hydrodynamic condition is modified by a mass-flow inlet to reach a high throughput isolation for the remain particles (4 and 12 μm diameter). The isolation percentages were 100 % for the microparticles of 25 μm, 18 μm and 12 μm, respectively. On the other hand, the isolation percentage of the microparticles of 4 μm achieved the 95 %.

articleTitle: Development of a Monitoring System for CO/CO2 with Android
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The accumulation of particles in internal environments has prompted research into developing monitoring systems for air quality. The environmental monitoring is done through atmospheric emission systems, they are high energy consumption and expensive. Therefore, the implementation of atmospheric systems is not a realistic technique for monitoring in internal environments. The use of commercial sensors for monitoring in internal environments is a challenge due to the lack of calibration, selectivity, sensitivity and architecture. For these reasons the objective of the papel are to develop a CO and CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> monitoring system with mobile application on Android. A Raspberry microprocessor Raspberry Pi connected to commercial sensors has been incorporated via cables, and wirelessly to an Android App. The sensors that were used are MH-Z19B for the detection of carbon dioxide CO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> and the MQ-7 for carbon monoxide CO. In order to perform the digital analog conversion between the MQ-7 sensor and the Raspberry PI Zero W, the ADS1115 component are added.

articleTitle: Usability Evaluation of Brain Computer Interfaces: Analysis of Methods and Tools
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Usability includes concepts such as satisfaction, efficiency and effectiveness. This may be partly the result of functionality, but they are mainly defined by the user's interaction with the system. The Brain-Computer Interface-BCI provides a direct communication path between the brain and the external world by translating signals from brain activities into codes or commands. The purpose of usability of BCI is that the interfaces can be understood, learned, used and be attractive to user, under specific conditions of use. For usability evaluation of BCI different methods (Questionnaires, Interviews, neurophysiological measures) and tools (VAS, QUIS, SUS, electroencephalography - EEG, functional near-infrared spectroscopy - fNIRS), magnetic encephalography - MEG) have been proposed. The evaluations are generally based on traditional methods (Questionnaires or Interviews), obtaining subjective answers without the certainty of the precision. In this paper an analysis of the usability evaluation methods of the BCI is presented.

articleTitle: Plant Location, Inventory Levels and Supply of Products to Areas Affected by a Natural Phenomenon
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In order to help organizations in the face of disaster in decision making, in this document was developed a model that combines the problem of the location of facilities for the establishment of a pre-positioned warehouse, the calculation of their inventory levels and the establishment of supply routes. The variability of the model with respect to the others lies in two variables: (1) finding a location that not only meets the minimum distance traveled characteristic, but also that possesses attributes that allow the proper management of the warehouse; and (2) the types of demand to those who focus on the products (food, equipment, water), are divided: early childhood, childhood, adolescence, adulthood and old age. The model is evaluated in one of the ten regions of the state of Veracruz, Mexico, called the Region of the High Mountains, with 57 municipalities, 27% of the total of the municipalities that make up the state and which has been the cause of the issuance of emergency declarations by the National Fund for Natural Disasters (FONDEN). The results show us that the location for the installation of the pre-positioned warehouse is located in the municipality of Fortín de la Flores, the order quantities, reorder point, safety inventory and shortage (in the form of kits) and the routes of delivery derived to the capacity of the vehicles used.

articleTitle: Cross-sectional study of digital competences in the school trajectory higher education students (e-skills)
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The need for evolution in the educational and technological part of higher level educational institutions is evident, as it is the last step for students oriented to their working life. Having the skills in digital knowledge is essential to expand their abilities and attitudes. In this research, we seek to identify the perception of students regarding the degree of knowledge and their reality, in relation to digital skills and their affinity towards them, in addition, it focuses on research methods to make a diagnosis of perception about digital skills of the students of the Facultad de Contaduria y Administración of the Universidad Veracruzana, and then, identify the transversality of the contents of the subjects and understand the current status. Starting from a methodology, conceptual and theoretical, allowed to analyze, under a deductive ways, the process of conceptualization and, later, its operationalization, where the evaluation dimensions are stipulated, with which an instrument with validity and reliability is presented, applied to a stratified sample to evaluate the five dimensions. The contribution of this research is based on the results of the statistical diagnosis, since with them you can generate strategies in the universities to identify the digital competences of the students and provide better tools focused on achieving a transversal objective in the school career, Implement new learning models and facilitate the acquisition of knowledge with better results.

articleTitle: Fall recognition system: a review
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: The World Health Organization (WHO) reports that between 28% and 35% of the population over 65 falls each year and the number increases as people get older. In order to improve the quality of life of older adults, the recognition of falls continues to be an area of active research. In this paper, we present a review of several systems for detecting the fall, including the sensors used to collect information in order to detect the fall, methods, datasets and results. Finally we present a discussion on possible future directions and challenges.

articleTitle: Perspectives of distributed and off-grid systems for the delivering of electricity to rural areas
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: This work studies the features of electrical renewable energy produced at small scale in rural areas and its use through distributed and off-grid energy systems. Recent trends in the application of these systems for the attention of needs of rural communities in several countries are reviewed. The study deals also with the paradigm that will soon affect the rural areas, when the demand of electricity in big cities reach critical levels requiring the availability of every power source, wherever they are, in order to give priority to the high demand in big urban centers, leading this way to an scenario of severe limitations in the energy consumption of rural communities.

articleTitle: Analysis of energy consumption due to electrical charging gadgets within educational facilities
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: An exploratory study was conducted to know how the students within the Faculty of Engineering of the Universidad Veracruzana use the electric power provided by the school. A group of them was consulted on the amount of equipment they use during their stay in the classroom. Likewise, a total energy consumption and its economic cost for the electricity bills of the university was calculated. In addition, a comparison of consumption of electrical equipment was made to verify the electrical power used inside the facilities to confirm the information provided by the manufacturer against the measured value of actual shape.

articleTitle: Data Fusion of Physical Variables as Bearing for User Thermal Comfort Analysis in Closed Environments
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: Context-aware systems use data obtained from variables, for example environmental, to adapt to changes in the environment. Due to this, it is necessary to analyze these variables to maintain healthy environmental levels and ensure users thermal-comfort in work spaces. In this sense, data fusion provides a way to unify data as a support for analysis of users thermal comfort. Thus, for this work, a sensor network was implemented to acquire data on environmental variables, such as temperature, humidity, air quality, light intensity, and noise level. While for the data fusion, Bayesian estimation was used as a method to generate knowledge about integrated values as a support for the analysis of users thermal comfort. This analysis was based on the specifications of the ASHRAE 55-2017 standard, which defines the thermal comfort zones according to users activities, and season. Results showed that the values of environmental variables were close to the thermal zone considered comfortable in summer for users. So, to improve thermal comfort conditions, other ventilation, cooling and air extraction systems could be installed in the work area. The importance of these analyses is to ensure a healthy and comfortable environment for users while performing daily activities.

articleTitle: Requirements Analysis for Tangible User Interfaces for Collaborative Use
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: On a requirements analysis process, software designers identify and collect information about users needs, requirements of the system and its user interface. In order to design user interfaces for collaborative use it is important to know what are functional requirements, individual and social users needs. This paper presents a process of requirements analysis for Tangible User Interfaces design, specifically for software that are used by a group of people working to achieve a common goal. The process followed to obtain requirements was based on Computer Support Cooperative Work perspective. As a case of study we considered the use of tangible medias in collaborative web design.

articleTitle: Production of biogas under thermophilic and mesophilic conditions of fruit and vegetable waste from the “Emiliano Zapata” market in Orizaba, Veracruz
publicationTitle: 2019 IEEE International Conference on Engineering Veracruz (ICEV)
abstract: In Mexico and the world, the final misapprehension and lack of integral management of Municipal Solid Organic Waste (RSOM) represents a problem of great environmental impact due to its inadequate disposal, production of bad odors and the attraction of vectors. The residues of fruits and vegetables are produced in large quantities at the markets and food distribution centers, these are a huge problem in the places where they are not controlled. The generation of RSOM in the city of Orizaba was 36832.66 tons in 2016, much of it generated by the city's markets; Countries continue to occupy a predominant place in the trade of goods, therefore, as generators of RSOM. In this research an alternative technology is developed to obtain biogas used for the management of organic media are used for the use of media. especially the accumulation of organic matter, in addition to determining the amount of biogas generated in thermophilic phase and another in mesophilic phase, the variation of COD, ST and STV, as well as pH at the laboratory level.
